title: SMALL EARTHQUAKE OVER-NITE
full_story:
The US Geological Survey recorded a small earthquake near West Salem early this morning.  The magnitude 3.5 tremor was recorded just after 2 am with an epicenter six miles northeast of West Salem.  The temblor originated from an estimated depth of 19.1 kilometers.  Minor shaking was recorded throughout the region.

The last major earthquake in the region was recorded April 18, 2008.  A slip along the Wabash Valley Fault triggered a magnitude 5.2 earthquake centered near Mt. Carmel.  That quake caused minor structural damage as far away as St. Louis.

title: NORTH CLAY SCHOOL BOARD
full_story:
At last weeks meeting of the North Clay School Board, Superintendent Keith Price shared information regarding the amended budget for FY26.  State, federal and local revenues and overall expenditures came in at the anticipated estimated amounts and the amended budget was approved.

Superintendent Keith Price also shared an update on district health insurance with the Egyptian Trust.  Due to the district’s low loss-ratio over the past two years, the district will have a 0% increase in employee insurance policies through Blue Cross-Blue Shield for the upcoming school year.  An update with the construction projects this summer was also shared.

The district renewed its agreement with Flora Public Library that provides a free library card to all North Clay students.  All North Clay students are encouraged to read this summer and take advantage of the resources and opportunities provided through this agreement.

In personnel matters the board hired Ben Rounds as summer custodian, Lindsey Fehrenbacher and Kyra Wagner as paraprofessionals, Rase Collins as Junior High School Assistant Softball Coach, Kyra Wagner as the Junior High School Cheer Coach, and to Post for 2 permanent substitute positions for the 2026-2027 school year.

title: FLORA 4th OF JULY
full_story:
Flora has a full day of events scheduled for Saturday the 4th of July with all of the events happening at Charley Brown Park.

At 10 am the All American Boy and All American Girl Contest will be on the Rotary stage.  The contest is for 3- to 7-year-old boys and girls and the deadline to enter is Wednesday.  Signups are available at the office of Lisa Erbacher Country Financial at 847 East North Avenue across from Rotary Park.

Kenzie’s Sweet Shop will also be on site at 10 am.  From 11 am to 6 pm free inflatables will be open for families, and from Noon until 4 pm the pool will be open for a free swim.  Flora Tourism will also be selling hot dogs and chips.  At 4 pm the food trucks will open, Poe’d Smoked BBQ, The Fair Lady, Colonel Pop, and Krazy Sweet Treats.  From 6 pm to dusk there will be live music by the Rewinds.

Everyone is welcome to bring a lawn chair and enjoy all of the activities.  There will be a shuttle service available to move people from the parking area to the attractions.

Fireworks will be at dusk featuring a 900 shot finale.  Please follow ESDA parking instructions.  Flora Tourism could still use a few volunteers.  To volunteer call Arriel Dulaney at the Chamber office at 618-662-5646.

title: CLAY COUNTY MOBILE HOME TAXES
full_story:
The 2026 Mobile Home Privilege Tax Bills are due on Wednesday.  For those who pay after Wednesday you will be charged an additional $25.00 per month.

If you did not receive a mobile home Privilege tax bill, and you own a mobile home, please contact the Treasurer’s office immediately at 618-665-3727 or email [email protected].

Clay County taxpayers can pay their mobile home taxes by mail by sending their check with the payment stub to the Clay County Treasurer PO Box 88 Louisville 62858.  Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date to avoid penalty.  Mobile home privilege tax bills can be paid at the Treasurer’s office in the Clay County Courthouse, they accept cash, check, cashier’s check, or money orders.  Please bring your entire bill if you want it stamped to show proof of payment.  The Clay County Treasurer’s office hours are from 8 am to 4 pm and they are open during the noon hour.  Payment can be made by placing payment in the envelope depository at the north entrance of the Clay County Courthouse.  Please include payment stub.  Tax Bills can also be paid online by credit/debit card by going to govpaynow.com PLC number a00082.

title: JULY BLOOD DRIVES
full_story:
ImpactLife will have a blood drive on Wednesday at the Iuka Fire Protection District from 4 to 7 pm.  Then there will be another blood drive at the Clay County Hospital on Thursday, July 9th from 10 am to 1 pm.  To schedule an appointment at either of these drives go to https://login.bloodcenter.org/donor/schedules/drive_schedule/144076

The American Red Cross is also making an urgent call for blood donors to book an appointment to give now to ensure hospitals stay ready to help patients without delay.

There will be a blood drive Friday, July 10th from 1 to 5 pm at the Clay County Health Department.  All donors who donate blood during this drive will get a American Red Cross Looney Tunes T-shirt.  Then there will be a Blood Drive at the Flora Oddfellows Lodge on Friday July 24th from 1 to 5 pm.  Donors at this drive will get a Fandango Movie Reward by email.

Donors, especially those with type O blood and those giving platelets, can help bolster the blood supply now by making an appointment to give in the coming weeks.  You can make an appointment to donate at Red Cross Blood Drives by downloading the free Red Cross Blood Donor App, visiting redcrossblood.org or calling 1-800-RED CROSS (1-800-733-2767).  Save time with RapidPass.  Complete your pre-donation reading and health history at RedCrossBlood.org/RapidPass or with the Blood Donor App before your appointment.

title: HOLY CROSS PARISH PICNIC
full_story:

title: COVER CROP FIELD DAY
full_story:
The Wayne County Soil and Water Conservation District is hosting a Cover Crop Field Day on Tuesday, August 18th at 4 pm at the Greg Dickey Farm in Wayne City.

Speakers will be David Kleinschmidt from Progressive Agronomy Consulting LLC,Torey Colburn from American Farmland Trust, and Dave Severin from the Illinois House of Representative.  There will be in field demonstrations, comparisons and a Soil Pit.

There will also be a meal for participants catered by Randy’s Smokehouse in Wayne City.  The Cover Crop Field Day is sponsored by the American Farmland Trust, Peoples National Bank and Farm Credit.

The Greg Dickey farm is located at 981 County Road 530, Wayne City, for more information call 618-842-7602 Ext 3.

title: COST OF GAS
full_story:
The average cost of regular gasoline and diesel fuel declined for a fifth straight week, prior to what is expected to be record travel during the Fourth of July weekend.

National prices Thursday averaged $3.91 per gallon for gas, down from $4.50 last month, and $4.95 for diesel compared to $5.59 last month, AAA reported.  However, the prices remain above year-ago levels of $3.22 per gallon for gas and $3.71 for diesel.

The recent downtrend in fuel prices aligns with a drop in crude oil prices.  The average price of Brent crude oil was back to a level last seen before the conflict with Iran.  Looking ahead, AAA projects a record 72.2 million Americans will travel more than 50 miles from home this week and over the holiday.

title: FIREWORKS SAFETY
full_story:
As Illinois families prepare to celebrate Independence Day, Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias released a public safety announcement urging residents to leave fireworks to trained professionals and attend organized community displays.

Giannoulias joined fire safety officials and medical professionals to highlight the serious injuries and tragedies that occur each year during Fourth of July celebrations.

“Fireworks are meant to bring people together and celebrate our nation’s independence,” Giannoulias said.  “But every year, emergency rooms treat Illinoisans suffering from severe burns, eye injuries and other life-altering injuries caused by fireworks.  The safest way to enjoy the holiday is to attend a professional display and leave the fireworks to the experts.”

“The use of pyrotechnics needs to be left to trained professionals,” said Lt. Jonah Kinsolving, Bomb Squad Commander for the Illinois Secretary of State.  “Fireworks do not always behave as expected.  A delayed detonation, malfunction or defective product can change someone’s life forever in a matter of seconds.”

Medical professionals warn that fireworks-related injuries often result in permanent physical and emotional trauma.

“We will see too many patients in emergency departments this holiday with injuries that were completely preventable,” said Dr. John C. Kubasiak, M.D., of Loyola University Medical Center.  “What may seem like a harmless activity can result in devastating injuries, particularly for young children.”

title: BUDGET ERRORS
full_story:
As the new state budget is set to take effect on Wednesday, Governor JB Pritzker recently used his item and reduction veto powers to eliminate $500.4 billion of spending, most of which was erroneously included in Illinois’ fiscal year 2027 budget.  $500 billion of that came from a single mistake that would’ve been given to an NAACP branch in Chicago.

Pritzker made the changes after consulting with the General Assembly’s Democrat budget leaders after the errors made it to the governor’s desk for his signature. However, State Representative Ryan Spain pointed to errors during debate in the final hours of the legislative session.

Because the Senate passed the spending plan after 3 am on June 1st and the House shortly after, the 3,700-page document lacked proper review.  The fast-tracked nature of the process has drawn heavy criticism regarding transparency, as lawmakers only had a few hours to review the sprawling legislation before the vote.
